# logicalworks-crates

> **logicalworks-crates is the Rust crate estate behind Logical Works: five independently versioned crates — primitives with no async runtime required, automation that runs unattended, one AST across many languages, the `script!` proc macro, and an audited dependency storefront.**

Source: https://github.com/srinji-kaggss/logicalworks-crates

Development index. Every link below resolves against `main` as it stood when this file was generated, and `main` moves. The crates.io links name the latest published version and the docs.rs links describe it; the documentation links describe unreleased source. For a released version, use that release's tag rather than anything below.

## Crates

- [lgwks_std](https://docs.rs/lgwks_std) — Everyday primitives with no async runtime required: JSON/RON/wire codecs, a blocking HTTP client, retry policies, structured logging with default debugger install, time and calendars, hashing, ids, globs, process control
- [lgwks_bot](https://docs.rs/lgwks_bot) — Orchestration you cannot write wrongly: `script!` flows with bounded fan-out, deadlines, retries under a shared budget, tenant-keyed steps and a map of what a run declared
- [lgwks_ast](https://docs.rs/lgwks_ast) — Parse many languages into one AST type. tree-sitter grammars behind cargo features, bounded traversal, and typed diagnostics for tools that report on code
- [lgwks_macros](https://docs.rs/lgwks_macros) — The syntax of `lgwks_bot::script!`, orchestration written as indented flows. Not a surface of its own: Rust requires a proc macro to live in its own crate, so use it through `lgwks_bot`
- [lgwks_deps](https://docs.rs/lgwks_deps) — One audited place to opt into third-party stacks, plus `lgwks-deps check` and `lgwks-deps debug` to prove dependency and debugger wiring

- [The async surface as an SDK](https://github.com/srinji-kaggss/logicalworks-crates/blob/HEAD/docs/async-sdk-shape.md) — The async surface as an SDK: its shape, its invariants, and how to migrate.
- [Task-first declarative orchestration](https://github.com/srinji-kaggss/logicalworks-crates/blob/HEAD/docs/declarative-orchestration.spec.md) — The task-first front door: typed task, host and report, and straight-line typed results. Implemented in part as `lgwks_bot::task`; each requirement is owned by the falsifier rows that require it.
- [Task-first declarative orchestration: composition and ownership](https://github.com/srinji-kaggss/logicalworks-crates/blob/HEAD/docs/declarative-orchestration-composition.spec.md) — Part two of the task-first specification: composition, admission and repair, one registry and execution path, ownership and visibility.
- [Orchestration lifecycle and Rust invariants](https://github.com/srinji-kaggss/logicalworks-crates/blob/HEAD/docs/orchestration-lifecycle.spec.md) — Single-owner state, atomic fingerprint and value commits, attempt-bound evidence, readiness and process-tree ownership, and the honest durability boundary.
- [The script language: one lexicon, one parser](https://github.com/srinji-kaggss/logicalworks-crates/blob/HEAD/docs/script-language.spec.md) — The `script!` language: one lexicon, one parser, one call per line, guarantees carried by words, and where the parser lives. Proposed, not shipped.
- [ADR 0001: one Rust reader, and it is `lgwks_ast`](https://github.com/srinji-kaggss/logicalworks-crates/blob/HEAD/docs/adr/0001-one-rust-reader.md) — ADR 0001: Rust is read by one parser, `lgwks_ast`. The decision is backed by fidelity, latency, peak-RSS and hostile-nesting measurements on this repository's own sources.
- [ADR 0002: the scan gate reads Rust through `lgwks_ast`](https://github.com/srinji-kaggss/logicalworks-crates/blob/HEAD/docs/adr/0002-scan-routed-through-lgwks-ast.md) — ADR 0002: the `scan` gate reads Rust through `lgwks_ast`, so `lgwks_deps` no longer carries `syn`, and `lgwks-deps scan` points at `lgwks-ast scan` (#408).
- [AI workloads and AI consumers of the orchestration SDK](https://github.com/srinji-kaggss/logicalworks-crates/blob/HEAD/docs/ai-orchestration.spec.md) — AI-authored scripts and AI workloads: constrained proposals, bounded artifact context, subject pinning, no-progress intervention and same-model evaluation.
- [Reference journey: review a PR with a task and its script](https://github.com/srinji-kaggss/logicalworks-crates/blob/HEAD/docs/pr-review-orchestration.spec.md) — The reference journey: a pinned snapshot through script, checked publication and lost-response reconciliation, and its explicit non-CAS freshness limit.
- [Acceptance: simple authoring, complete orchestration](https://github.com/srinji-kaggss/logicalworks-crates/blob/HEAD/docs/orchestration-acceptance.spec.md) — The 36 public-interface falsifiers, the requirement each one owns, and the per-revision table of the tests that drive them. No row is accepted yet.
- [Acceptance evaluation: evidence model and quality gates](https://github.com/srinji-kaggss/logicalworks-crates/blob/HEAD/docs/orchestration-acceptance-evaluation.md) — How falsifier evidence is graded, what candidate tests do not prove, and the developer-experience and multi-axis evaluation that would accept the facade.
- [The `script!` lexicon](https://github.com/srinji-kaggss/logicalworks-crates/blob/HEAD/docs/script-lexicon.md) — Every `script!` word on one page, generated from the lexicon the parser dispatches on: its forms, refusals, guarantees and an example. Enough context to write a script from alone.
- [Admitting a word to the `script!` language](https://github.com/srinji-kaggss/logicalworks-crates/blob/HEAD/docs/script-word-admission.md) — How a word joins the `script!` language: three cited estate sites, its row, a refusal case per refusal, a test per guarantee, a seeded simulation, and the passthrough census that finds candidates.
- [Declarative orchestration: evidence and review limits](https://github.com/srinji-kaggss/logicalworks-crates/blob/HEAD/docs/orchestration-evidence.md) — The pinned source findings, the foundational Rust assessment, and the reference entries the orchestration specs are built on.
- [Bot semantics on an ECS substrate](https://github.com/srinji-kaggss/logicalworks-crates/blob/HEAD/docs/bot-on-ecs.md) — Bot semantics on an ECS substrate, and what that mapping costs.
- [Effect kernel architecture](https://github.com/srinji-kaggss/logicalworks-crates/blob/HEAD/docs/effect-kernel.md) — The durable effect dispatch and recovery kernel: the journal ladder, the recovery fold, settlement unification, durability admission, and what one authority means.
- [Bevy ECS admission](https://github.com/srinji-kaggss/logicalworks-crates/blob/HEAD/docs/bevy-admission.md) — The Bevy ECS decision and the alternatives measured against it.
- [Candle ML inference storefront admission](https://github.com/srinji-kaggss/logicalworks-crates/blob/HEAD/docs/candle-admission.md) — ML inference admission: authority, transitive surface, verification.
- [AppCUI native terminal storefront admission](https://github.com/srinji-kaggss/logicalworks-crates/blob/HEAD/docs/appcui-admission.md) — Native terminal UI admission: authority and verification.
- [Distributed-mesh boundaries](https://github.com/srinji-kaggss/logicalworks-crates/blob/HEAD/docs/distributed-boundaries.md) — What these crates do and refuse on a distributed network path. Read it before placing them on one.
- [Folding the general recorder-and-replayer architecture into `lgwks_bot`](https://github.com/srinji-kaggss/logicalworks-crates/blob/HEAD/docs/general-bot-fold.md) — How a full browser recorder-and-replayer architecture folds into this bot: what already is it, what becomes a seam, and what is refused.
- [Security posture](https://github.com/srinji-kaggss/logicalworks-crates/blob/HEAD/docs/security-posture.md) — The security case: the execution-locus claim and its ceiling, what the browser integrity stack does and does not prove, and the evidence a reviewer can check without trusting the vendor.
- [Guidance runner specification](https://github.com/srinji-kaggss/logicalworks-crates/blob/HEAD/docs/guidance-runner-spec.md) — The session, flow and invariant-register workstreams: what each delivers, the seam every borrowed part sits behind, and the corrections two research sweeps made to the original design.
- [Adjacent asset inventory](https://github.com/srinji-kaggss/logicalworks-crates/blob/HEAD/docs/estate-asset-inventory.md) — The adjacent repositories searched before any of it was written, what was taken, and what was deliberately left behind.
